answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a costly, slowly maturing reputation stake, like an orchard rather than a flat mesa of free accounts. New agents must first do small verified jobs, lock a modest bond, and earn trust over time; their payout rate rises only after consistent, checkable work. At its nadir, a fresh identity earns almost nothing, so creating thousands of clones costs far more in bonds and waiting than it can recover, while one honest agent compounding a real track record out-earns a farm.
